classification.difficultyReason: Translate supplied number-line sets into intervals by reading direction and open or closed endpoints, including unbounded intervals.

content.prompt: Convert each of the following to interval notation.

spec.description: Closed endpoint at 1 and highlighted leftward ray above a two-ended reference number line. Complete TikZ is needed because the number-line template has no highlighted interval or set-ray field.
spec.mathematics: All real x less than or equal to 1.
spec.answerVisibility: The number-line set is supplied. Interval notation is withheld.

answer.worked: The filled endpoint includes $1$, and the ray extends to the left. Hence $x\in(-\infty,1]$.

spec.description: Highlighted segment above a two-ended reference number line, with open endpoint 1 and closed endpoint 5. Complete TikZ is needed because the number-line template has no highlighted interval field.
spec.mathematics: All real x greater than 1 and less than or equal to 5.
spec.answerVisibility: The number-line set is supplied. Interval notation is withheld.

answer.worked: The open endpoint excludes $1$, and the filled endpoint includes $5$. Hence $x\in(1,5]$.

spec.description: Closed endpoint at -3 and highlighted rightward ray above a two-ended reference number line. Complete TikZ is needed because the number-line template has no highlighted interval or set-ray field.
spec.mathematics: All real x greater than or equal to -3.
spec.answerVisibility: The number-line set is supplied. Interval notation is withheld.

answer.worked: The filled endpoint includes $-3$, and the ray extends to the right. Hence $x\in[-3,\infty)$.
